planned.title: Larger exercise
planned.prompt:
Two arrays contain 64 distinct IDs each. One is sorted and one is shuffled. Choose the array where a midpoint value comparison can safely eliminate a side, and explain why.
For the ideal model that halves the candidate count each step, how many halvings leave one candidate? Derive the general relation between starting size n and halving count k.
planned.answer: Choose the sorted array. Order lets a midpoint comparison rule out the side whose values cannot match. After k ideal halvings, n/2^k = 1, so k = log₂(n). Starting with 64 gives 6 halvings. This counts ideal halvings, not the exact comparisons of a particular implementation.
planned.reason: Start with a connected task. Its separate criteria may show useful strengths and gaps without a prerequisite quiz.
